instruction: In the Slide Master view (accessible via View > Master > Slide Master), change the slide number's font color to black

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Paraphrased version with black color - parenthetical navigation hint. The evaluator uses the existing check_page_number_colors function which parses the slide master XML.
metadata.verification: The check_page_number_colors function from slides.py (lines 876-920) parses the slide master XML to find the color of the page number placeholder. It checks the second-to-last solidFill/srgbClr element in the slide master and verifies it matches the expected color using threshold-based RGB comparison (red: R > G+50 and R > B+50, blue: B > G+50 and B > R+50, green: G > R+50 and G > B+50, black: R < 50 and G < 50 and B < 50).

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator uses check_page_number_colors which extracts the second-to-last solidFill/srgbClr element (index -2) from slideMaster1.xml. This is a hardcoded positional assumption that is fragile and overfitted to specific XML structures.

The function does not semantically verify it is reading the page number placeholder - it simply assumes the second-to-last color element corresponds to the page number without checking placeholder type or name.
Color matching logic for black uses threshold < 50 for all RGB channels, which is reasonable but may not handle all edge cases (e.g., very dark grays vs pure black).
The postconfig correctly saves the file with Ctrl+S, ensuring the modified PPTX is persisted before extraction.
Despite the fragile extraction logic, the evaluator will likely work correctly for this specific task and file (saa-format-guide.pptx), as indicated by the metadata verification note.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Make the color extraction logic more robust by searching for the page number placeholder by name/type (e.g., <p:ph type="sldNum">) rather than using hardcoded positional index -2.
Add validation to confirm the extracted element actually corresponds to the slide number placeholder before checking its color.
Consider making the black color threshold configurable (currently hardcoded as 50) to handle different interpretations of 'black' color.
